item.title: 'RedZone' returns for 18th season and, despite 15-second commercials, could still be on in the White House
item.description: Scott Hanson confirms 'RedZone' will air limited 15-second commercials between plays this season, but promises fewer ads than last year's count
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's popular "RedZone" broadcast returns for its 18th season on Sunday, and while the focus is seemingly on how many commercials the previously commercial-free program will air, host Scott Hanson has other things up his sleeve.

But first, the commercials thing:

"There will be, there will be what people define as commercials," Hanson told OutKick recently. "The plan is right now to have a limited number of 15-second commercials only in between plays.

'NFL REDZONE' HOST SCOTT HANSON SAYS HE UNDERSTANDS FAN FRUSTRATION OVER COSTLY STREAMING SUBSCRIPTIONS

"So we're on a Dallas Cowboys drive. OK, first-and-10 after a 5-yard gain. They're walking back to the huddle. That's when we will splice in one standalone, 15-second commercial. I can confirm that for you."

"RedZone" aired 16 advertisements of some kind at one point last season, which marked a significant increase for what was once seven hours of commercial-free programming.

Hanson said fears that the number will increase to start the 2026 season are unfounded. In fact, there will be fewer at the start of the season. That, of course, says nothing about what will happen later this season, but Hanson isn’t making those decisions.

"The rest of it is up to the business folks and Uncle Scott doesn't make the decisions when it comes to the business folks at the NFL," he said. "But yes, there will be advertisements, a limited number, what I would describe as a limited amount, but fans can make their own minds up about that."

Fans made up their minds about "RedZone" and Hanson a long time ago, and those fans have come from some unlikely places.

"I've been told we've been on in the White House in the last two administrations, so both sides of the aisle," Hanson said.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

"I've been told by the players ... Tom Brady, loves ‘RedZone,’ loved it when he was a player, when he was playing on Monday Night Football or Thursday night football or the bye week, he was watching ‘RedZone.’

"Josh Allen — one of the faces of the NFL today — loves ‘RedZone.’ When he's playing on an off day or whatever, if he can watch ‘RedZone.’ So it's just, it's, it's a phenomenon."

Hanson, back with Lowe's for the second year of the popular "Earn Your Sunday" campaign along with Dak Prescott, Christian McCaffrey and Justin Jefferson, is something of a renaissance man.

He's visited six of the planet's seven continents and promises to eventually make it to Antarctica, the only continent he's missed.

Hanson has cage dived with great white sharks and found himself at somewhat safe distances from lions on the Serengeti. He's also visited the Great Wall of China.

All that begs some rapid fire questions:

So, what's his adventure vacation preference, running with the bulls in Pamplona or climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?

"I've done both," Hanson said. "Kilimanjaro was more beautiful. Running with the bulls required more courage. Running with the bulls."

More afraid of great white sharks or lions?

"Lions, because you don't have bars in front of you when you go on safari in the Serengeti plain," Hanson said. "I had bars in front of me when the great whites came up."

Because he visited both China and Mexico, we have to ask: Mexican or Chinese food?

"Oh, Mexican," Hanson said. "Only because in China, the Chinese food is not like American Chinese food. Let me just tell you that I ate a thing called duck dong. And I'm like, what is duck dong? I like it, it's real tasty, until they slowed down, and I learned they were speaking English, and they were saying duck tongue.

"Duck tongue is what they were feeding me. Yeah, no. Give me Mexican."

Seven hours of RedZone begins at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

item.title: Former Bond girl says next 007 should be 'another gorgeous man' as James Bond decision
item.description: Alison Papworth weighed in on who should play James Bond in the iconic film franchise. The actress appeared in "For Your Eyes Only" and "Octopussy."
item.content:encoded:
The search for the next 007 is underway, and former Bond girl Alison Papworth has a clear message: leave one thing untouched.

"What do I hope? I know they’re about to announce the next Bond, aren’t they?" the actress, who also works as a director for a London-based design and consultancy firm, told Fox News Digital. "And we’re all waiting with bated breath."

"If they’re true to the books, I hope it’s a man," she said. "A man, just a man. Yes, I think it would be very strange if it were a woman. Don’t you? It would be a totally different thing. So I hope it’s another man, another gorgeous man."

AMAZON ANNOUNCES SEARCH FOR NEXT JAMES BOND IS UNDERWAY, AS HOLLYWOOD CASTING CHOICES COME UNDER SCRUTINY

Papworth’s comments came before Gary Oldman said on "The Morning Show" that his "Slow Horses" costar Jack Lowden could be the next James Bond.

"Jack, it’s been rumored that he’s on the shortlist," Oldman said on the Canadian talk show. "We’re going to find out pretty soon, aren’t we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack."

According to Deadline, Oldman later clarified his comments, saying: "There’s six people on a shortlist. I heard a rumor that they’ve picked James Bond, but they haven’t announced it yet, which is their prerogative. So I do not know [who has got the part], but I’m hoping it’s Jack."

Amazon MGM Studios gained creative control of the James Bond franchise in 2025 after forming a joint venture with longtime Bond producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli.

WATCH: BOND GIRL ALISON PAPWORTH REVEALS HER HOPE FOR THE NEXT 007

In May, the studio announced that the search for the next James Bond was underway. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next installment, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Daniel Craig last played 007 in 2021's "No Time to Die."

People magazine reported that Paul Mescal, Jacob Elordi and Jack O'Connell are among the actors rumored to be in the running to take over the iconic role.

The upcoming release will be the 26th Bond film in the more than 60-year-old franchise.

Papworth appeared in 1981’s "For Your Eyes Only" and 1983’s "Octopussy," both of which starred Roger Moore.

"He was an absolute gentleman," she said. "Yes, I know everybody says it. I only have fabulous, fabulous memories of him being funny, telling the best jokes. Very dry, very droll."

"One thing I really remember about him, when we were in India, there was a stuntman, I think it was a stuntman. He used to smuggle beef drippings in his luggage for Roger because he loved it. It was very funny, and it stuck in my mind all those years later."

Being a Bond girl had its benefits. Papworth recalled being flown first class to Rio de Janeiro, where vodka was flowing for the cast, and she tried caviar for the first time. In between filming, she would observe Moore playing Backgammon at picture-worthy destinations.

But life on set wasn't always as luxurious.

"It was the middle of winter doing the scenes for 'Octopussy' where we were fighting in the castle," Papworth recalled. "We learned to stunt fight, and it was supposed to be in India. But we were at Pinewood Studios, and it was below freezing. All the girls had these red bodysuits on with big capes. We were so cold, we had thermals on underneath, so we probably looked about five pounds heavier."

Papworth didn’t expect to appear in two Bond films. She recalled a publicity director once telling her, "Once you’ve done a Bond movie, you get thrown on the Bond Girl scrap heap." But Broccoli, daughter of longtime Bond producer Albert "Cubby" Broccoli, had a different idea.

"You can imagine my surprise when I got the call from Barbara Broccoli saying, 'You’re on the next one, Alison,'" she said. "And it stayed with me. Bond has stayed with me. It’s changed my life. My two best friends, I met one on 'For Your Eyes Only,' Vanya Seager; she was another Bond girl. And I met my other best friend, Carole Ashby, on 'Octopussy.' Carol was there when my baby was born. Vanya and I, we speak every day. I speak to them both every day."

"So without Bond, I wouldn’t have those two incredible bonds," she added.

After appearing in two Bond movies, Papworth continued acting and modeling. By the time she reached her 30s, however, her modeling career was "leveling out."

"My husband had lots of properties, and I’d always loved interior design," she said. "I’m totally self-taught, but I’m passionate about it. And he just started giving me properties to do, and that developed into our business, which has been running successfully for all these years. I still love it. And after he died, I carried on. He taught me well."

Today, Papworth is a director at Camhall Design & Consultancy, an interior design company based in the U.K. It has completed projects in London, New York, Boston and the Bahamas. She also helped launch Lustre & Lustre London, which offers "luxury cleaning services."

Papworth and her close pal, Joan Collins, also teamed up to raise funds for Shooting Star Children's Hospices. According to the organization's site, it supports, "babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions, and their families, across south-west London, north-west London and Surrey."

Papworth still has fond memories of her time bringing the Bond stories to life.

"I love show business," she said. "I really do. It’s fabulous. And maybe I’m lucky that I’m not super famous, so I can have a private life. I’m not like my dear friend Joan who gets stopped everywhere. I’m lucky because I can dip in and out of it."

"I still do signings," Papworth continued. "It went quiet through my 30s and 40s. And then, I don’t know. Bond fans are very good at tracking you down. I started to get invites to do signings. I remember doing my first signing in Birmingham at this huge exhibition center. My husband and my kids came because I was a first-time signer. There were all 'Star Wars,' 'Doctor Who,' astronauts, boxers, and little me."

item.title: Human vs ChatGPT in NFL Week 1 betting picks, from Bears and Packers to Texans and Lions
item.description: The Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers and Washington Commanders headline a human-vs.-ChatGPT NFL betting showdown with 10 total Week 1 picks.
item.content:encoded:
I’m not sure why I keep doing this to myself, but I’ve decided to spend the NFL season going head-to-head with ChatGPT in a battle of betting picks.

Each week, I’ll make my five best NFL bets. Then ChatGPT will make its five best bets from the same odds board. We’ll track both records throughout the season and let the results determine who actually knows what they're talking about.

2026 NFL SEASON PREDICTIONS: DIVISION WINNERS, PLAYOFF TEAMS AND SUPER BOWL PICK REVEALED

I expect ChatGPT to wipe the floor with me. It has access to more information than any human could process, while I have a long and proud history of giving people reasons to bet against me. If it can’t beat me, all those people predicting AI will take over the world are clearly wrong.

The lines used will be the best available numbers when the picks are made. I reserve the right to complain that I was on the right side and just got unlucky, but the record will count the same either way. If ChatGPT gets one wrong, however, it wasn’t unlucky. It was just wrong. No moving the goalposts for the robot.

First up: my five picks. Then, ChatGPT’s five picks.

Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers, 1 p.m. ET (FOX)

I don't love laying three on the road in Week 1 but the Bears are a team on the rise that came within a play of reaching the NFC Championship last year. The Panthers made the playoffs, but they weren't all that good and are due for negative regression.

Solid price on the better team, and Chicago’s offense should match up well with Carolina’s zone-heavy defense. The concern is laying a full field goal on the road with several Bears carrying injury questions.

Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars, 1 p.m. ET (CBS)

Simple: where are the points going to come from? Deshaun Watson and the Browns? Well, maybe, but only if it's Watson throwing pick-6s or turning the ball over deep in his own territory. I also like getting a few unders on the card because Week 1 unders are 52-28 (65%) over the past five seasons, including a 12-4 mark last year.

Cleveland’s quarterback and offensive-line uncertainty create a very low scoring floor; the danger is Jacksonville or its defense producing most of the points.

Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles, 4:25 p.m. ET (FOX)

I'm expecting a big bounce-back from Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders this season and I think it starts in Week 1. The addition of Stefon Diggs gives the team another weapon and it's going to matter against Philadelphia. The Eagles, conversely, seem primed for a step back and I'm concerned about Jalen Hurts leaning on DeVonta Smith as his No. 1 receiver.

CONTROVERSIAL PREDICTIONS AND RANKINGS OF ALL 32 NFL STARTING QBS JUST IN TIME FOR REGULAR-SEASON KICKOFF

This is the pick I like least. ESPN’s FPI still favors Philadelphia by 4.8 points, which creates only a thin numerical edge on Washington +5½, but its weakened offensive line against Philadelphia’s defensive front could overwhelm that advantage.

Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders, 4:25 p.m. ET (FOX)

I don't have a lot to say here because it's roughly the same as the Browns-Jaguars analysis. I don't see either team scoring much, especially with Malik Willis and Kirk Cousins guiding these two offenses.

Strong pick—Brock Bowers’ absence and Miami’s unsettled offense give both teams low scoring floors.

Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS)

I almost feel like a sucker taking this bet because it feels like the most obvious play on the card. But how can I not jump on the better team as an underdog against a team starting another new quarterback this season? I think Kevin O'Connell is an excellent coach and Kyler Murray will thrive under him, but I think it will take a few weeks to come together.

Packers moneyline is my favorite pick on your card and our only overlap. ESPN’s FPI favors Green Bay outright, although the absences of Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs make it far from comfortable.

For full transparency, I used GPT-5.6 Sol Max mode, fed it the OddsChecker board as it appeared Saturday at 6 p.m. ET and gave it the following prompt:

"I’m writing an article in which I go head-to-head with you, ChatGPT, on NFL bets. Here’s how it will work: Pick your five best bets for Sunday based on the odds provided. No bet can be priced worse than -120. Review every spread, total and moneyline that falls within those parameters and determine whether it belongs among your five picks. Explain exactly why you’re selecting each of the five bets. Also explain exactly why you're passing on the eligible bets you don't select."

THESCORE BET PROMO CODE: GET A $1000 BET RESET AHEAD OF THE OPENING NFL SUNDAY OF THE 2026 SEASON

GPT took nearly 20 minutes to produce these five picks:

Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans, 1 p.m. ET (CBS)

Houston’s defense is healthy and has repeatedly troubled Josh Allen. ESPN’s FPI projects Buffalo by only one point—still a Houston cover—while most ESPN and NFL.com panelists picked Houston outright. I prefer the points over Houston’s moneyline at +105 because a one-point Buffalo win cashes the spread.

Projection: Houston 21, Buffalo 20

I hate this pick. Sorry, but I just can't bet against Josh Allen and the Bills, especially in Week 1. Houston won nine straight games to end the 2025 regular season, but they mostly beat up on bad teams and, yes, they beat the Bills but it was a home game on a short week. Even their playoff win was against a mediocre Pittsburgh team.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals, 1 p.m. ET (FOX)

Fifty-one points is a demanding Week 1 threshold. Both defenses added personnel, both starting quarterbacks barely played during the preseason and Tampa Bay’s receiving depth is compromised. ESPN analyst Ben Solak recommended the same under at the worse price of -112.

Projection: Cincinnati 26, Tampa Bay 23

I don't hate this look at all. As mentioned, unders are typically hot in Week 1 and this game screams OVER given the two offenses. Usually when a pick seems obvious, take the other side. In this case, that's the under. Good pick, GPT.

New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions, 1 p.m. ET (FOX)

Detroit averaged 28.3 points last season and has recently been the league’s most productive home offense. New Orleans brings weak pass protection, has ruled out Cameron Jordan and lists Alvin Kamara as questionable. Exactly seven pushes, so I would not play -7½.

Projection: Detroit 31, New Orleans 20

Well, this is the other side of the obvious coin. I feel like the public is going to hammer Detroit. I wouldn't be confident betting against the Lions, but I don't love laying the seven, either. I'd avoid this one, personally.

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS)

ESPN’s FPI projects a 9.6-point margin, and four of NFL.com’s five projected scores cover -9. Arizona allowed 35.2 points per game over its final nine games last season and now has two secondary starters out.

Projection: Chargers 30, Arizona 17

Again, I just hate laying these huge numbers in Week 1. The public loves big favorites and we just don't know enough about these teams to lay more than a touchdown. This is an avoid for me.

Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS)

ESPN’s FPI gives Green Bay a 56.8% win probability, while +110 requires only a 47.6% win probability. Jordan Love finished 2025 third in Total QBR. The moneyline also strictly improves upon Green Bay -½ at +106: It pays more and pushes on a tie.

Projection: Green Bay 24, Minnesota 23

Well, since I also made this bet, I'm obviously a fan. Great job, GPT. Or, more likely, terrible job since my picks are notoriously bad.

But we’ll see. Check back next week to see how we both did. Follow along throughout the season as we try to answer the most important question currently facing the United States of America: Who is better at betting the NFL, humans or robots?

item.title: Paige Spiranac golfs and talks about hooking up in college, Ava Hunt on game day & a brawl in WVU's blue lot
item.description: Paige Spiranac revealed on her YouTube series she "dabbled in college" while playing golf with comedian Andrew Santino as they discussed dating.
item.content:encoded:
What a weekend and the best part is that it's not over yet. And this is coming from a guy who spent all day yesterday without any air conditioning where the temperature reached a high of 86.

Not to mention the fact that I learned the A/C unit simply didn’t stop working on Friday night because of a simple fix. Nope, the unit is dead and it needs to be replaced.

We also learned we would be sweating out another night sleeping with whatever relief a couple of fans provides. But I'm still looking forward to Sunday because we'll have cold air by the end of the day, and even better than that, it's the first Sunday of the NFL season.

Add the Oregon and Ohio State losses to the fact that we have our first full slate of NFL action, and I'll gladly be a little uncomfortable for a few more hours.

Before we get into those losses by the Ducks and Buckeyes, we're going get Sunday Screencaps started by heading out to the golf course where Paige Spiranac is talking about dating in college.

GOLFER PAIGE SPIRANAC LEAVES PLAYING PARTNER SPEECHLESS WITH AWKWARD QUESTION, LLWS MUD & WNBA WIKI PAGES

I can't believe it hasn't been mentioned already, but let's see what golf's top influencer had to say last week when she faced off with comedian Andrew Santino for her YouTube series "Paige Meets Her Match".

During part one of their one on one match, Santino asked Paige who she would take back to her cabin at the Celebrity Invitational, assuming everyone there was single. You know, typical golf course talk.

PAIGE SPIRANAC GIVES PEOPLE WHAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW THEY NEEDED: HER YOGURT BOWL RECIPE

"Sarah Winter … she's the best looking one there," she said, reports the NY Post.

"Really? You’re a ladies lady," Santino responded. "Have you ever dated a girl?"

Paige answered that while she didn't date women, she "dabbled in college … Hooked up."

A natural follow-up question was asked. Would she date a woman, and she replied, "I think so."

That's spending time productively on the golf course. They're having fun. They're playing golf and they're making some content. And they're also getting to the bottom of some romance by asking the tough questions.

If that's not golf, I don't want it.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS

The first is a touching story of revenge. Last September, Oklahoma State visited Eugene, Oregon and was handed a 69-3 loss for their troubles.

This year, the Cowboys played host in Stillwater, Oklahoma. They weren't about to allow a repeat of last year. The No. 6 Ducks weren't leaving with a win. They were going home with the worst upset loss of the week.

The schedule doesn’t get any easier for Oregon either. They're taking on Portland State next week in a true test of what they're made of.

Can they beat a team of Portland State's caliber after losing to an unranked Oklahoma State? We shall see.

Similar questions will be asked of Ohio State, who entered play on Saturday ranked No. 1 and left with a one-point loss after blowing a big lead to Arch Manning and the No. 4 ranked Texas Longhorns.

Can the Buckeyes get back on track against Kent State at home? That's not a guarantee after blowing a 20-point fourth quarter lead in Austin. It's going to come down to whether they're disciplined enough to handle their business.

I get that not every team can remain focused enough to give up only nine points through their first two games of the season, like Penn State has done. But if you're truly a top ten team, you shouldn't lose that game to Oklahoma State.

And a true No. 1 travels to Texas and plays the entire 60 minutes or however long they play football games in Austin. You never know where a hidden clock will pop up next.

We have to ask after that win over Ohio State. Is Texas back? They might be.

Speaking of hidden clocks with magical seconds on them, Michigan got their first win of the season. They defeated the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners at home.

Good for them. We'll have to see if they're back on the right track next week when UTEP visits Ann Arbor.

item.title: White Sox amateur scouting director Mike Shirley resigns on heels of verbal harassment allegations
item.description: Mike Shirley allegedly made racial and sexist comments at the Area Code Games, leading to his resignation as Chicago White Sox scouting director.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago White Sox amateur scouting director Mike Shirley has resigned, with the organization announcing the news on Saturday prior to the team's 6-5 win against the St. Louis Cardinals.

Shirley, who was in his seventh season in the leadership role, was alleged to have made inappropriate racial and sexist comments about coworkers and in front of coworkers, according to The Athletic.

The report said that Shirley was placed on administrative leave after an anonymous tip was made to the White Sox regarding his conduct at the Area Code Games in Long Beach, Calif., in August. The Area Code Games is a scouting event that welcomes high school players and is attended by scouting directors, other scouting personnel, as well as front-office employees.

LOS ANGELES ANGELS FIRED ADVANCE SCOUT NICKNAMED 'BASEBALL SPY' AFTER HE WAS CAUGHT FILMING ROCKIES

Chicago's latest investigation into Shirley also included allegations of vulgar language about females and their bodies, sources told The Athletic.

It is the White Sox's policy not to comment on personnel decisions, according to MLB.com.

Shirley had been the subject of at least one other internal investigation in the past in which an anonymous tip was reportedly received from a former White Sox employee who claimed to have left their role regarding Shirley's behavior toward scouts "from underrepresented groups," The Athletic reported.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Shirley did not receive any disciplinary action after the investigation reportedly found no wrongdoing.

The 56-year-old was named the director of amateur scouting for the White Sox in September 2019 after serving as an assistant scouting director and a cross-checker from 2010-2018.

Shirley and his department's work this year was highly focused on Chicago holding the top pick in the MLB Draft for just the third time in franchise history.

The White Sox, who also held a record Draft pool of $20,489,500, selected shortstop Roch Cholowsky out of UCLA at first overall. Chicago shut down Cholowsky for the remainder of the season in August, citing right wrist soreness.

item.title: ‘Family Affair’ star Kathy Garver says failed remake ‘sucked,’ reveals what went wrong
item.description: Kathy Garver called the 2002 "Family Affair" remake terrible, saying Gary Cole and Tim Curry couldn't replicate the original cast's deep warmth.
item.content:encoded:
Kathy Garver is not holding back about the failed 2002 remake of "Family Affair."

In a new interview with Fox News Digital, Garver — who is gearing up to celebrate the 60th anniversary of "Family Affair" by hosting a special marathon featured on Catchy Comedy — explained why the reboot lacked the chemistry, warmth and familial bond that made the classic show so beloved.

"Excuse my language, but it sucked," Garver, who portrayed Cissy in the original series, said. "And it did for many reasons."

'FAMILY AFFAIR' STAR TALKS 'SURVIVING CISSY,' SEEING ANISSA JONES FOR THE LAST TIME AND ALLEGED SITCOM CURSE

The original "Family Affair" premiered in 1966 and followed bachelor Bill Davis as he unexpectedly became the guardian of his late brother and sister-in-law's three children: Cissy, Buffy and Jody. Brian Keith played Bill, while Sebastian Cabot portrayed the family’s butler, Mr. French.

The 2002 remake featured Gary Cole as Bill Davis and Tim Curry as Mr. French. Although Garver praised both actors, she said they brought entirely different qualities to the characters audiences had already grown attached to.

KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES

"I think it’s very difficult to do a remake," Garver said. "When they see Gary Cole, they say, ‘Well, that’s not Uncle Bill.’"

Cole was "great in ‘NCIS,’" Garver said, but "as you know, he’s no Brian Keith."

Keith’s appeal, she explained, came from the contrast between his tough exterior and his tenderness toward the children.

Brian Keith was "this macho guy, the ex-Marine," Garver said. "And here he is, this loving dad."

TIM CURRY'S CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED

Garver also felt Curry’s portrayal of Mr. French was too far removed from Cabot’s understated performance.

"Tim Curry had a whole different take on it," she said. "It was very good, but it wasn’t in a situation-comedy vein. It was like the Tim Curry show."

"And so that didn’t quite mesh with Sebastian Cabot, who was a wonderful actor," she added.

Garver described Curry’s Mr. French as "loud and boisterous," while Cabot’s version was "much more low-key."

ORIGINAL 'LITTLE HOUSE' VILLAIN RETURNS FOR REBOOT WITH WARNING FOR NEW NELLIE

Cabot’s performance was also rooted in his character’s love for the children, Garver said — something she felt the remake failed to convey.

"He, too, did everything in love," she said. "And basically, he loved the children. And I think that was missing from Tim Curry."

WATCH: ‘FAMILY AFFAIR’ STAR KATHY GARVER SAYS FAILED REMAKE ‘SUCKED,’ REVEALS WHAT WENT WRONG

The actress said the original cast members brought an authentic sense of family to the show because their characters genuinely cared for one another.

"Each individual person on the original ‘Family Affair’ had a family that they loved," Garver said.

‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS

Garver credited that emotional connection with helping the show stand out from other sitcoms of its era.

"I think it was a groundbreaker," she said. "It was the first of its kind — a single father, or a single uncle, single relative, that all of a sudden gets three orphan children."

The series also benefited from its production quality, according to Garver. She noted that "Family Affair" was among the early television sitcoms filmed in color and that many of the cast and crew members came from the movie industry.

"So it was a real quality kind of show," she said.

Garver said the original series also featured "relatable characters" and storylines that continue to resonate with audiences.

"It has stories that endure today," she said. "And so it remains relatable, I believe, because it’s a family. And how — what do I do with the family? How do I deal with these problems? And it shows you that."

She also believed the warmth of the original series was reflected in the way the characters interacted with one another.

item.title: ‘Food divorce’ trend among couples could drive them apart, experts warn
item.description: The "food divorce" trend has some couples eating separately, but experts warn the growing trend erodes relationship quality and emotional well-being over time.
item.content:encoded:
Between differing diet plans, food intolerances and conflicting work schedules, some couples are choosing "food divorce" — a term circulating on social media for partners who intentionally cook, order and eat their meals separately.

While taking separate paths at mealtime might solve logistical headaches, experts warn that splitting up at the dinner table can come at a cost to the relationship.

Shared family meals can help people reconnect, build stronger emotional bonds and reduce stress, according to health institutions like Mayo Clinic. 

‘QUIET QUITTING’ IN MARRIAGE: THE SUBTLE SIGNS A SPOUSE HAS EMOTIONALLY CHECKED OUT

For couples, experts say regularly eating apart could become a concern if it reflects broader emotional distance or reduces opportunities to spend meaningful time together.

Nutrition experts emphasize the issue is often less about the food itself and more about the lost opportunity for a built-in daily checkpoint.

"I think it reflects many people's very busy schedules," Tanya Freirich, a North Carolina-based registered dietitian nutritionist, told Fox News Digital.

"Mealtime can be a time to unite, to communicate, to build social relationships and foster a connection," she said. "If we're eating completely alone or at different times than important people in our lives, it may foster a little bit of disconnection."

DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE

Eating separately can contribute to a "roommate dynamic," experts note. Without regular time to reconnect and discuss the day, couples may have fewer opportunities for communication.

The practice can also contribute to isolation, according to Freirich.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Communities all around the world for thousands of years have come together around mealtimes," she said. 

"If so many Americans are eating every meal alone for many days or most of their days, that certainly can't be great for mental health or well-being."

There can also be practical drawbacks, as preparing separate meals or ordering from different restaurants may increase grocery costs, preparation time and kitchen cleanup.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Additionally, eating solo can impact individual dietary habits. Studies show people dining alone are more likely to eat quickly, mindlessly scroll on their phones, or settle for heavily processed convenience foods compared to when they share meals with others.

Couples can accommodate different dietary needs without preparing entirely separate meals. 

For those navigating specific calorie targets, plant-based diets or medical restrictions, Freirich recommended building "modular" or "choose your own adventure" meals as a more efficient method.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Something like a deconstructed taco night, grain bowls, a pasta or noodle night, or even a sheet pan meal where you're creating each food on its own," the expert said. 

"So the protein, the carb, the veggies are being cooked separately. And then you get to decide your portions and make your own meal from those ingredients that can meet everyone's needs."

When conflicting schedules or caregiving duties make daily dinners impossible, experts recommend prioritizing quality over frequency. 

Even sharing a quick weekend breakfast or setting aside one designated night a week can help maintain connection.

"Be very intentional to connect when you can," Freirich suggested.

"Make that a really special meal. Be intentional with your connection. Put the phone away and actually enjoy the other person's company."

item.title: Hollywood producer spent 25 years praying for Tinseltown, says 'you can't hate them'
item.description: Faith-based Hollywood Prayer Network celebrates 25 years of praying and creating community for entertainment’s storytellers.
item.content:encoded:
Hollywood is a place many Christians have condemned; Karen Covell has spent 25 years asking them to pray for the people who work there instead. She is the founder of the Hollywood Prayer Network and sees the town as her greatest ministry.

After all, screenwriters themselves have long preached the maxim "story is everything," and if stories create meaning, influence emotions and shape identity, then Hollywood is the most influential mission field there ever was.

That’s what Covell was thinking when she began the faith-based organization that, along with her staff and now 170+ chapters in 42 countries, just celebrated its 25th anniversary with a Gatsby-themed gala in downtown Los Angeles.

FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT

Founded in 2001, the Hollywood Prayer Network, through prayer, community and resources, supports the entertainment industry’s storytellers and believes the next generation of actors, writers, directors and producers doesn't have to maneuver Tinseltown alone.

The organization offers everything from intercessory prayer and professional discipleship programs to networking and Bible studies.

"We have a beautiful community here. You couldn't get me out of this place for anything because the people that are here are wonderful," Covell told Fox News Digital.

It was more than 25 years ago that Covell, along with her composer husband, Jim Covell, saw and felt the need for believers in Hollywood to have support.

KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE

"It's competitive, a lot of people look for work, we're all freelancers, and we wanted to support the people of faith here who really felt like they had one foot in the church and one foot in the Hollywood entertainment industry and neither one liked each other," Covell, who originally came to Los Angeles to attend the University of Southern California, explained.

While the two had already started a prayer group, they found that those coming to Los Angeles out of the church arrived in the city, as she put it, already "beat up."

SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’

"I knew Hollywood didn't like the church because we were really terrible to them — we boycotted, we threw out our TVs, we burned their books — we wouldn't go to their movies, you know, but I believed if you pray for somebody, you can't hate them," Covell said.

She recalled hearing stories from people in the group whose families, pastors and friends had warned them not to go to Los Angeles — that it was Satan's pit and that they couldn't live there.

HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER BEHIND 'APOLLO 13' REJECTS POLITICS IN HIS MOVIES, SEEKS TO UNITE AUDIENCES

"And I said, ‘This is ridiculous. We should be storytellers, we should be creative. God created us to be creative.’"

So Covell decided to try to figure out a way to build a bridge between the church in America and Hollywood.

NEARLY 500 PUBLIC FIGURES FROM POLITICS TO HOLLYWOOD WILL READ BIBLE COVER TO COVER TO MARK AMERICA'S 250TH

"I thought, ‘I've got to get the church to start understanding the beauty and the importance of Hollywood,’" she said.

Since then, whether someone is a believer or not, the HPN has prayed for people ranging from fledgling singers to the likes of Britney Spears during her periods of intense tabloid scrutiny and personal struggle. Paris Hilton has received intercessory prayer while Robert Downey Jr. was lifted up during his public battle with addiction. There have been many prayers for wildlife, crisis relief efforts and, recently, for celebrity blogger Perez Hilton following his distressing livestream and subsequent hospitalization.

NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD

Through its monthly Kids Prayer Calendar, "Ones2Watch," members support child and teen actors in prayer before they face major industry pressures.

The organization has established numerous community groups geared toward directors, dancers, writers, comedians and people working in technology and AI. It has local chapters across the United States, each serving entertainment professionals through mentorship, networking and worship. It also has its own app, which lists its resources, local chapters around the world and community events.

"We have gatherings of people all over the city and all over the country and the world who say, yes, it's important to be storytellers," Covell said, noting that she has found what really attacks artists is isolation, discouragement and fear. "Those three things can all be combated in community."

For her part, Covell credits her 42-year marriage to a husband who counts the days they’ve been together as a big part of her own success. The two, who recently finished a book titled "Confessions of a Hollywood Marriage," as she put it, "pray together every day and walk with each other through the hard and good times."

"It's not a how-to book, it's not anything to help people, it is just us telling the story of our marriage and how it's been such a beautiful and amazing journey for the last 42 years," Covell said. "It's not because we're any different or special… We know people see so many bad marriages that they lose hope that it's possible. And we just let people know, this is the greatest gift."

Just last year, Covell chose to step down from producing and instead devote herself fully to the Hollywood Prayer Network, which she said has been growing quickly of late.

It wasn’t that way at the start.

"I take credit for having, I think, the slowest-growing ministry on the planet. It was just one person at a time. Would you pray for Hollywood?" Covell quipped. "And I just kept going."

Recently, staff and members posted a video on the organization’s social media showing Covell jokingly preparing for a "Netflix documentary" about what it’s like to be a Christian in Hollywood. The viral posts included disclaimers clarifying that the Netflix part was just a ruse based on a popular online video trend.

Covell just wants to keep supporting storytellers as they tell great stories and reminding them that they’re not alone in the process.

"… As a producer, I worked in Hollywood and in the secular industry. My husband is still writing music in the secular industry. We love the commercial industry of Hollywood. We love the people, we love the projects, we love the place," she said. "This ministry started growing and I slowly started seeing other people come with the same feeling of, ‘Well, let's build community. Let's be together. Let's love the people we're here with. Let's celebrate being storytellers.’"

"We want to tell great stories that inspire people, that encourage people. And we want to know that we're not alone doing it. So, that's my purpose with the prayer network."

item.title: Dan Dakich says women might be the reason for Nike's downfall: 'They p----d them off'
item.description: Dan Dakich says Nike's collapse stems from alienating women buyers and losing ground to Athleta and Lululemon in a booming competitive market.
item.content:encoded:
It's no secret at this point that Nike is taking a nosedive.

They're being mercilessly mocked online for releasing a low-effort series of NBA jerseys, and their stock has plummeted so much that they are set to get the boot from the S&P 100 later this month.

While plenty of personalities have weighed in, OutKick's Dan Dakich decided to throw his hat in the ring and discuss just how bad things have gotten for the failing athletic apparel giant.

OUTKICK'S CRAIG CARTON REVEALS THE REAL REASON NIKE STOCK IS IN THE TANK: 'THEY'RE FAILING MISERABLY'

On a recent episode of his "Don't @ Me" show, Dakich was joined by Dan Zaksheske and Jason Hammer to break down the missteps committed by Nike that led them to this lowly state.

Zaksheske opined that the "go woke, go broke" mantra certainly applies here, but we have to take everything into account, including complacency.

"I would compare Nike to Disney," Zaksheske stated. "They're just resting on their laurels. They're not creating anything new."

Hammer offered a different perspective, giving credit to FOX Business's Taylor Riggs for the insight.

TED CRUZ TAKES VICTORY LAP AS ICONIC AMERICAN BRAND'S STOCK PLUNGES TO 12-YEAR LOW

"They gave a middle finger to the retailers," he said. "They thought they could go directly to the consumer and that didn't work, coming out of a COVID-era where people were desperate to actually go out and go to the stores, see the displays, and the Nike displays weren't there anymore."

Dakich certainly agreed with his guests, but he offered his own take on the matter.

"Local competition," he said when pointing a finger at Nike's problems. "Athleta is booming. Lululemon is booming. It used to be Nike or Adidas, which one are you going to buy?"

Competition in the marketplace can either force you to improve or make you watch from the sidelines, and Nike seems to be doing the latter.

Alienating the local retailers was a big mistake from Nike, but Dakich posits that the company has a female problem, too.

"Women have said, 'Bulls---, don't insult us,'" Dakich said. "Who's buying stuff? It ain't me and it ain't you (Hammer)... it is freaking women, and (Nike) p----d them off."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

There's no doubt that Nike is facing a litany of issues, and Dakich, Zaksheske and Hammer only scratched the surface of what appears to be a catastrophic crossroads for the former kings of athletic wear.

If they want to climb back to the top of the mountain, they will definitely have to look in the mirror and do some soul-searching.

Only time will tell if that happens before it's too late.

item.content:encoded:
I wish I had an opening line that was memorable like Scott Hanson over on Red Zone. We have hours of uninterrupted football, and our first full schedule. My first play of the weekend comes as the Dolphins take on the Raiders.

The Miami Dolphins are my pick to earn something really special this year… the #1 overall draft pick. That’s not exactly a good sign, but I do think they will be the worst team in football. The Dolphins team has been decimated over the course of the past year. Their coach from last season: gone. Their starting quarterback from last season: gone. Their top wide receivers (Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle): gone and gone.

Is there any hope for optimism in this game? De’Von Achane is still one of the better running backs in the game. Malik Willis is dynamic and has shown flashes of success in both Tennessee and Green Bay. At the same time, Achane might not have any running space considering the teams know he is the best and only true threat on the team. Willis has shown flashes, but he has also shown that he is normally a backup quarterback for a reason.

The Las Vegas Raiders also underwent many changes this offseason. They earned the #1 overall pick last year with a terrible season of their own. That saw them dismiss Pete Carroll and bring in Klint Kubiak to take over the franchise. It also saw them select Fernando Mendoza with the first pick, and then they also grabbed Kirk Cousins, who worked with Kubiak previously.

The Raiders tried to trade away Maxx Crosby in the offseason, but that was vetoed, and he is now back on the roster. He should still be solid for the club, but there are questions around the rest of the defense. Their new coach is also not a defensive guy, so there is reason to be concerned about this side of the ball. For some context, the Raiders are ranked 24th in the league for defensive line rankings. The Dolphins are 30th. Brock Bowers is out for the game, and that hurts the Raiders, but I think it will be okay against the Dolphins.

KIRK COUSINS AND NO 1 PICK FERNANDO MENDOZA GIVE RAIDERS BETTORS SOME HOPE IN THE UPCOMING YEAR

We have two quarterbacks in new spots, and questionable defenses. Does that mean we will get a high-scoring game, or will the quarterbacks be too busy trying to figure things out? Personally, I think we get the higher-scoring game, but I’m not touching the total. I don’t think there is enough on one side or the other to really invest in it. I do lean toward the over 40.5, though.

Instead, I’m backing the Raiders at -3 in this one. Las Vegas is one of the teams that I think will improve, but let’s not believe that they will win a ton of games. They are still going to miss the playoffs. There are still a lot of questions. But for one game, the Raiders should win the game by at least three points, and I think they should win by five or more. Back the Raiders.

item.title: College football’s chaos era is here: Texas rallies, Oregon falls and Lane Kiffin eyes return to Ole Miss
item.description: Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss with LSU looms after a chaotic week saw Arch Manning rally Texas past Ohio State and Oklahoma State stun Oregon.
item.content:encoded:
If you were waiting for chaos to encompass college football, the second week of the 2026 season delivered in a chaotic way on Saturday.

We started the day with Michigan taking down No. 11 Oklahoma in the Big House, and ended it with No. 5 Texas pulling-off a 20-point comeback to shock No. 1 Ohio State in what might turn out to be one of the wildest fourth quarters we witness this season.

ARCH MANNING AND TEXAS LONGHORNS ERASE 20-POINT DEFICIT TO STUN OHIO STATE IN SHOCKING COMEBACK FOR THE AGES

But, in the middle of what was a remarkable day in the sport, Oklahoma State decided to create pure madness in Stillwater in their win over No. 6 Oregon that sent shockwaves through the college football world.

Look, we knew it was going to get a little wild this season. But, the Ducks falling this early in the season, to the Cowboys?

This turned out to be a rough day for the Big Ten conference, even with Michigan taking down the Sooners in Ann Arbor. You know, just how we thought it would go, right?

No.

I've seen a collapse before, but what we witnessed on Saturday night in Austin, Texas, was shocking.

The Buckeyes held a 23-3 lead entering the fourth quarter, and everything we had seen up until that point had Ryan Day heading back to Columbus with a monster win.

But, it turns out the football gods had other plans for everyone either watching inside DKR Stadium or at home.

It was Arch Manning that led a struggling Texas offense from the ashes, just after the internal speaker system finished playing 'Dont Stop Believing' throughout the stadium. I guess this wasn’t the cheesy moment those within the pressbox thought it would turn out to be.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

All it took was for the Longhorns to somehow slow down Jeremiah Smith just enough for them to start putting together enough momentum to steal this one from the Buckeyes. Manning led Texas to three drives that spanned over 10 plays each for touchdowns, sending Ohio State fans who made the trip into a state of shock.

"I had nightmares about that game," Arch Manning said after leading his team to the comeback win about last year's game.

This one will obviously be remembered for a very long time, especially within the Texas fan base. Just when you thought the Longhorns were buried, somehow these Longhorns found a way to steal one from the Buckeyes.

As for Oregon, I have no idea how Dan Lanning explains this one. Oklahoma State had lost 21-straight games to FBS opponents.

OKLAHOMA STATE STUNS OREGON, DEALS EARLY SEASON BLOW TO DUCKS' NATIONAL TITLE HOPES

This is the same Oklahoma State team that lost to Tulsa last weekend, with new head coach Eric Morris getting the biggest win of his career so far. For the Ducks, losing 39-31 is one thing, but folks should also remember this Oregon team scored fourteen of their points off turnovers.

So, it's not as if Dan Lanning's team was flying around all afternoon in Stillwater. An expensive roster can’t save you if the team is not fully prepared for every game. On Saturday, the Oregon Ducks found out the hard way, and now we can throw out all Big Ten predictions in the process.

Prepare yourself now, because the next six days are going to center around Lane Kiffin making his return to Ole Miss with his LSU Tigers.

Sure, we've got SMU vs. Louisville, Houston versus Texas Tech, along with a few other intriguing matchups.

But nothing will touch the cinema that will take place in Oxford, Mississippi.

There will be hatred, language, non-stop security surrounding Kiffin as he roams the LSU sidelines, and we still haven’t discussed everything that will encompass next week in the SEC.

We've waited almost ten months for Kiffin's return to Ole Miss, which was discussed on what felt like a daily basis during the offseason.

Now, we are here. The spotlight is finally shining on what should be the wildest college football environment we see this season, for all the insane reasons you might imagine.

I know you've been waiting, Ole Miss fans.

Your former coach is headed back to town, and all eyes are on this family reunion in Mississippi.

item.title: Democrats punish members who put working Americans ahead of party loyalty
item.description: Jared Golden and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez broke ranks with House Democrats to advance a Maine lobster bill and a resolution condemning socialism.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats in Washington have committed the party’s newest unforgivable offense: representing the American people. Democratic Reps. Jared Golden, of Maine, and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, of Washington, broke with their party Sept. 1 to advance a procedural rule allowing the House to consider Golden’s Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act and a resolution condemning socialism. The rule passed 210–208, with five Republicans opposed, making their votes decisive.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other Democratic leaders accused them of blindsiding the caucus, called their decision a "significant breach of trust" requiring a "serious response," and asked the Committee on Caucus Rules to review the matter. Think about the political message Democrats sent: Helping Maine lobstermen fight burdensome regulations and allowing Congress to vote on a resolution condemning socialism are now acts of political blasphemy inside the Democratic Party.

Democrats will insist their outrage is about House procedure and not lobstermen. That distinction doesn’t matter to most Americans who expect their representatives to protect their livelihoods. Golden co-sponsored legislation to protect Maine’s half-billion-dollar lobster industry, which supports thousands of workers and coastal communities.

JEFFRIES THREATENS 'SERIOUS RESPONSE' AFTER DEMOCRATS HELP GOP ADVANCE ANTI-SOCIALISM VOTE

Gluesenkamp Perez represents a southwest Washington district where families also depend on fishing and natural-resource industries. Both chose workers over mandates they believed were impractical. Golden captured the absurdity: "Could you imagine going home to your constituents and being like, ‘I was trying to help you, but I had to vote no’?" That is precisely what Democratic leaders demanded, put the party before the people who elected you.

The timing of this vote and the Democratic Party’s reaction are politically dangerous because most Americans consider themselves working class. A recent Pew Research Center analysis found that 60% of adults say "working class" describes them extremely or very well, up from 54% in 2024. That includes half of college graduates and half of upper-income Americans, while the figure rises to 77% among blue-collar workers.

FRUSTRATED BLUE-COLLAR UNION BOSSES RIP SOCIALIST POLITICIANS, WARN OF LABOR EXODUS FROM DEM PARTY

This identity cuts across income, race and education, making it one of the broadest political constituencies in America. These voters may not follow House procedure, but they understand the lives of fishermen, farmers, tradesmen and small-business owners. These are everyday Americans who Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez defended. By treating their defense of working people as betrayal, Democratic leaders directly exposed a party that places partisan loyalty and ideology ahead of the working class.

That reaction is particularly risky because Democrats hold a fragile advantage on the cost of living, which is the leading midterm issue. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found that voters prefer Democrats over Republicans by 36% to 28% on handling this issue. However, 37% chose neither party or remained unsure, suggesting Democrats are benefiting from frustration rather than confidence in their economic plan. By punishing members who defended workers, Democrats are giving Republicans an opportunity to define them in four words: Democrats are against you.

DEMOCRATS ARE IN BIG TROUBLE BECAUSE BLACK AND BROWN VOTERS DON’T WANT SOCIALISM

That opening grows even wider when Democrats are forced to defend their economic ideology.

The House passed a resolution condemning socialism, but 192 Democrats voted against it while only eight joined Republicans in support.

The House passed a resolution condemning socialism, but 192 Democrats voted against it while only eight joined Republicans in support. Democrats argue that the measure also included Republican election-security provisions. Four Democrats even proposed condemning socialism in a separate amendment stripped of those provisions, but it never received a vote.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That may explain the objections of those four Democrats, but it does not explain the other 188. Democrats want voters to trust their economic agenda while refusing to draw a clear line between their policies and socialism. Worse, members who defend workers or challenge the party’s progressive direction now face punishment. Democrats may campaign as the party of working people, but their policies favor greater government control.

Republicans must make the consequences of that agenda tangible for every American family. America prospers when people are free to work, build, fail, recover and pursue the American Dream without government permission. Greater government control brings higher taxes, heavier regulations and rising costs, ultimately leaving workers, families and small businesses with less money, less freedom and fewer opportunities. Democratic leaders have revealed their priorities: The party comes first and working Americans come last. In November, working Americans will have the final word.

item.title: GOP women sound alarm as Lindsay Clancy backlash revives calls to repeal 19th Amendment: ‘Definitely a threat’
item.description: Republican women warn that online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment after the Lindsay Clancy trial could alienate female voters from the GOP.
item.content:encoded:
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Calls to repeal women’s rights to vote are emerging from the online firestorm over the Lindsay Clancy trial, prompting Republican women to warn that the intraparty rhetoric could hurt the GOP.

"I think there’s definitely a threat in the Republican Party right now," political and legal strategist Mehek Cooke told Fox News Digital.

The online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment come after Clancy’s high-profile murder trial ended in a mistrial, with 11 of the 12 jurors favoring a verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity. Clancy admitted to killing her three children, but her defense argued that she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN

"Convict Clancy. Also Repeal the 19th Amendment!" one user posted on X.

"The female jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial are speaking out about their deliberations and disagreements with the sole male holdout. The more they speak the better they make the case for repealing the 19th Amendment," posted another user.

Cooke warned that calls to strip women of the right to vote, largely coming from accounts identifying as conservative, risk alienating female voters from the Republican Party.

"When you have these fringe activists online talking about repealing the 19th Amendment or alienating women, it really doesn’t help," Cooke said.

The calls followed after the case made waves on social media, particularly after hundreds of mostly female Clancy supporters gathered outside a Massachusetts courthouse during the murder trial. The demonstrators rallying behind Clancy argued the case is an example of the lack of understanding of postpartum depression.

ROGAN SHREDS SUPPORTERS OF LINDSAY CLANCY, SAYS THEY WOULDN'T RALLY IF A FATHER WERE ON TRIAL FOR SAME CRIME

But the demonstrations quickly turned into ammunition for online critics who argued that the support for Clancy is an indication that women should be stripped of their right to vote.

"This Lindsay Clancy trial has shown us How spiteful women can be, the fact that women are willing to even defend a child killer just because they want to be ok with the "sisterhood" should alarm you," another user wrote on X.

The post continued, "They will gaslight you, they will use sign language against you and even try to call you all sort of names. But guess what, they are still wrong and they know it. Repeal the 19th."

Cooke pushed back on the idea that the calls to repeal the 19th Amendment reflect the reality of the mainstream Republican party.

"Social media isn’t real life," Cooke said. "I think a lot of people out there put these arbitrary crazy ideas, but it doesn’t really reflect what normal people think and what mainstream thinks."

LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL BECOMES SOCIAL MEDIA OBSESSION AS TIKTOKERS, SLEUTHS DEBATE CONTROVERSIAL CASE

She continued, "I think you're getting these calls because of where our culture is today. You looked at the Lindsay Clancy trial and all the women out there in pink that were continuing to support a woman who murdered three children. You're constantly seeing this cultural push in terms of where women stand today in politics."

Tiffany Losee, director of fundraising for The Conservative Caucus, told Fox News Digital that Democrats are to blame for pushing out this agenda and associating it with the broader Republican Party.

"You have to understand this is all a game to the Democrat Party," Losee said. "They’re going to push out anything that looks fringe on the right."

Losee also claimed that Democrats are using this rhetoric on the right to distract voters from the rise of socialism that has emerged within the Democratic Party, claiming if voters understood the ideals of the party they would "run faster than imaginable to get away from such government control."

HOW THE 'LONG MARCH' THROUGH THE INSTITUTIONS LED TO SOCIALIST TAKEOVER OF DEM PARTY: 'NEED TO WAKE UP'

"They're gonna push out crazy, Lindsay Clancy ideas, or ‘look over here at something shiny, or communism is cool, socialism is cool, everything's free,'" Losee said. "But then they will not take that extra step to educate the voter on what exactly they are pushing."

Cooke and Losee spoke to Fox News Digital on the issue as Republicans gathered in Dallas for the party’s first-ever midterm convention, where the GOP gathered to rally their base to vote as Republicans work to stay in control of Congress as November’s midterm elections approach.

"I think the left has constantly alienated women," Cooke said. "It's our responsibility to pull them in and show them common sense."

item.title: Georgia killer who murdered two suburban real estate agents faces execution after 23-year wait for justice
item.description: Lori Brown's mother recalls the 2003 Powder Springs murders of two real estate agents as Stacey Ian Humphreys' Georgia execution date nears.
item.content:encoded:
As the execution date nears for a Georgia man convicted of killing two real estate agents, the mother of one victim is remembering the women who were murdered while simply doing their jobs, and the risks that real estate professionals still face.

Barring a last-minute judicial stay or executive clemency, Stacey Ian Humphreys, 53, is scheduled for execution on Sept. 16 at the Georgia Diagnostic and Classification Prison in Jackson.

On Nov. 3, 2003, Lori Brown, 21, and Cynthia "Cyndi" Williams, 33, were working from a model-home office inside the Oakwind subdivision, a rapidly growing, upscale residential development in Powder Springs, when Humphreys fatally shot them.

The office welcomed prospective buyers, making interactions with unfamiliar visitors a routine part of their professions.

74-YEAR-OLD BECOMES FLORIDA'S OLDEST INMATE EXECUTED AFTER 1982 KILLING OF TEEN

Williams returned to the office after lunch and encountered Humphreys first. Brown arrived shortly afterward and unknowingly walked into an armed robbery already underway.

Humphreys held the women at gunpoint, made them strip, and killed them before fleeing with their ATM cards. There was no evidence of sexual assault.

Ed Greathouse, a retired supervisory investigator with the Cobb County Judicial Circuit who assisted the prosecution, told Fox News Digital that investigators never determined why Humphreys chose that particular office over others in the development.

For Brown's mother, longtime real estate agent Linda Brown, her daughter’s outgoing personality made her a perfect fit for the profession.

"Let me tell you, she was a rascal growing up," Linda told Fox News Digital. "She had a gregarious spirit about her."

"She was a people person from the time she was small. She never met a stranger. That's why real estate was such a perfect place for her because she was really good at it."

Brown formed a close friendship with Williams, who took Brown under her wing. She also planned to marry her high school sweetheart in 2004. She had been tasting wedding cakes and looking at venues, Linda said.

On the day she was killed, her wedding-planning notebook sat neatly on her office desk.

"Sometimes I think it's my fault. I should have never let her go in this direction with real estate but, you know, she was going to do what she was going to do," Linda added.

After the murders, Humphreys used the stolen bank cards to withdraw over $3,000, according to court records.

On Nov. 8, 2003, authorities arrested Humphreys in a rental Jeep Grand Cherokee, following a high-speed chase in Wisconsin. Investigators found the murder weapon inside the rental, along with Williams' blood on the gun. They found Brown's blood inside Humphreys’ personal vehicle, according to the Georgia Supreme Court record.

Greathouse said investigators believed Humphreys was heading toward Canada when a Waukesha County officer apprehended him.

"It was fairly common knowledge in prison, where he had been, and certainly in law enforcement, that if you get to Canada, Canada won't extradite you back to the United States, unless the prosecutor absolutely will not pursue the death penalty," he said.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Although Humphreys insisted he did not remember killing the women, he told investigators, "I know I did it. I know it just as well as I know my own name."

Authorities learned that Humphreys was behind on his vehicle payments and had taken out a high-interest payday loan he could not afford.

In 2007, a Glynn County jury convicted Humphreys of two counts of malice murder, along with armed robbery, kidnapping and aggravated assault. He pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

THREE DEATH ROW INMATES EXECUTED BY LETHAL INJECTION IN RARE SAME-DAY STRING ACROSS US

The state scheduled Humphreys' execution for Dec. 17, 2025, but the State Board of Pardons and Paroles postponed the date and his clemency hearing amid legal challenges.

Greathouse said obtaining a death sentence was unusual during his years working capital cases in Cobb County.

"I did 13 death penalty cases in Cobb County during my tenure, and that was, I think, one of two we actually achieved the death penalty," he said. "It's really rare."

Nearly 23 years after her daughter’s death, Linda remains skeptical that Humphreys' execution will take place.

SEND US A TIP

"Not only did we lose these two girls, but we had to go through 4.5 years waiting for a trial to come to an end. So, here we are 23 years later," she said. "I’m still in favor of the death penalty for this man that took their lives."

Humphreys' attorney filed a motion this past week to try to throw out his death sentence over claims of jury misconduct, but a judge rejected that motion on Thursday, FOX 5 Atlanta reported.

GOT A TIP?

Linda continues to speak about the case during National REALTOR® Safety Month, an initiative held every September to raise awareness about safety risks in the profession.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"A lot of my friends had said to me at that time, ‘We know you'll probably want to get out of real estate,’" Linda said. "I thought about it a long time, and I decided that I was not going to let this man drive me out of my profession."

Linda said she avoids taking clients into basements or putting herself in places where she could become cornered, and she walks behind prospective buyers while showing homes.

"I'm not saying that what happened to Lori and Cyndi, that they could have done anything different from what they did. They were very vulnerable."

item.title: Zachary Levi calls California a ‘failed state’ that is ‘literally and figuratively on fire’ after Texas move
item.description: Zachary Levi calls California a "failed state" after leaving Hollywood for Texas. The 'Chuck' actor is starring in Guy Moshe's new action-thriller 'The Fix' opposite Liam Neeson.
item.content:encoded:
Zachary Levi isn't holding back about why he packed up and left his home state of California for Texas.

In 2017, the 45-year-old actor, who is starring in the upcoming action-thriller "The Fix," sold his home in Los Angeles and bought a ranch outside of Austin.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital alongside his "The Fix" co-star Liam Neeson, Levi candidly opened up about why he left the Golden State.

KIRK CAMERON PRAISES NASHVILLE'S 'GOOD VALUES' AFTER DITCHING CALIFORNIA OVER COST OF LIVING, POLITICS

"I grew up in California, I love California, it is a failed state," he said. "It is literally and figuratively on fire."

Along with his disillusionment with California, the "Chuck" star explained that his departure was rooted in a long-standing desire to rethink how the entertainment industry operates from the inside out.

NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE'

"Ever since I started working in Hollywood and I saw how broken it all was, I felt very compelled by God to go build a better Hollywood — like a new United Artists kind of studio — where it's owned and operated by the artists, where we can cut out all the middlemen, where we all can do really well, build a community," Levi said.

"And then not just a place to work," he continued. "People can live there and kids can go to school there and we have an organic farm and like all of the things that I think everybody really wants these days."

WATCH: Zachary Levi calls California a 'failed state' after moving to Texas

'FRIDAY NIGHT LIGHTS' STAR ADRIANNE PALICKI SAYS TEXAS GAVE HER SOMETHING HOLLYWOOD COULDN'T

"We look at the regular world around us and we see it burning and we're like, 'Can we do this better? I feel like we can do this better," Levi added. "So that all culminated in nine years ago, me finding 75 acres outside of Austin, Texas to buy, to develop, to turn into this magical kind of idea. That's why I left."

Levi is fulfilling his vision by building Wyldwood Studios, a $100 million film and lifestyle campus on his 75-acre property in Bastrop County outside Austin.

PARAMOUNT ESCALATES THREAT TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA AS DEM AG'S ANTITRUST LAWSUIT STALLS WARNER BROS MERGER

Designed as a hybrid production hub and creative retreat, the multi-phase project pairs soundstages and production offices with residential housing and wellness spaces. Wyldwood is expected to open its first two soundstages in 2027.

Looking back on his decision to move, Levi explained that walking away from his life in California meant trading idyllic weather and close personal ties for a bigger mission.

‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STARS JEP AND JESSICA ROBERTSON SAY ‘A LOT OF PRAYER’ LED THEM TO LEAVE LOUISIANA FOR TEXAS

"I left behind a lot of community and family and perfect weather in Southern California, but when you weigh it all out and you must, you have to come to these points in your life and you go, 'Is all of that really worth the thing that I know I'm supposed to go build in the future to make a better world?' And to me, that calling on my life was more important," he said.

"Fortunately, Austin's awesome. It's great, you know?" Levi continued. "It can get kinda hot in the summer and kinda cold in the wintertime, but I can deal with it."

"There's no thing as bad weather, just the wrong clothing," he added.

"The Fix" marks a sharp departure for Levi, who is best known for starring in lighter projects like the action-comedy series "Chuck" and the superhero film franchise "Shazam!"

TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS

Directed by Guy Moshe, the movie follows a group of war-torn, disgraced former CIA operatives, led by Tucker (Levi) and mentored by his long-time lead Larry (Neeson), who are left disillusioned in the chaotic wake of the 2021 U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan.

After a high-stakes mission goes disastrously wrong, the team embarks on a rogue, high-risk mission in Tehran. Seeking both a life-changing score and a chance at personal redemption, the group attempts to pull off a daring rescue operation while confronting their own past choices.

TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S $330M FOUR SIXES RANCH PURCHASE FORCED HIM OUT OF RETIREMENT PLANS

While speaking with Fox News Digital, Levi explained that he was drawn to the project because he wanted to take on a different character type than those that he had previously played.

"I wanted to do something fun, gritty, darker, in comparison to other roles that I've played in the past, and this gave me that and then some, because there was all of the great spycraft and twists and turns and revelations throughout the story, as well as this human foundation," he said.

Levi continued, "'Who are these people in real life? Why are they doing the things that they're doing? What is this redemption that they are trying to seek?' The moral ambiguity of all of that, of like, who's really the good guy and who's the bad guy. I think these are really cool themes to explore. And I got to do them with the Liam Neeson."

While speaking with Fox News Digital, Neeson also explained why he joined the movie's cast, heaped praise on Levi along with Moshe, who co-wrote the screenplay with Mark Bacci.

"It is a terrific script," he said. "Really, really good, talented director and writer."

"He's a wonderful actor," Neeson added of Levi. "I'm not just saying that because he's here, but he is wonderful."

Along with Levi and Neeson, "The Fix" also stars Annet Mahendru, Grant Harvey, Augusto Aguilera, Elnaaz Norouzi and Wes Chatham.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, Moshe explained that he believed from the outset that Levi was a natural fit for the project and wasn't surprised by how hard the actor pushed himself physically for the role.

"When I met him, I immediately asked myself, ‘How am I the first one to see what a great action star this guy can be?’ Like a 6'4, handsome, commanding, almost like old movie star type of kind of presence," Moshe said.

"But to me with Zach, the nice thing about him is which people, I think, don't know as much about him — he's a very much of an outdoors person," he continued. "He lives in Austin, Texas on the ranch. He likes rafting. He likes to be outside. He likes to hike. I mean, he's a very physical person in real life."

WATCH: ‘The Fix’ director Guy Moshe says Hollywood overlooked Zachary Levi as an action star

"And he embraced it and was every bit a collaborator from day one," Moshe added. "So I wouldn't say surprised but rather validated, maybe is the word that I could use. Like I believed that this would be the case when I met him and he clearly exceeded my expectations even here."

Moshe told Fox News Digital that Levi brought a raw, real-world edge to the set that surprised even the filmmakers.

"Let's just say I found myself in the streets of Tbilisi in a fist fight with Zach and I throwing punches, with people in the middle of the street, which is maybe not something I should advertise," Moshe said. "But I don't know if people would expect that of him. But like he's quite a man's man in that capacity."

"He's done all these movies where it's like the four-quadrant family films, all that kind of stuff, whatever, but he's certainly, I think, a much more intense person in real life in certain ways that people might not be familiar with," the director added.

Norouzi also praised Levi during her interview with Fox News Digital. In "The Fix," the Iranian-born German actress plays Zara, a woman recruited to pose as the Persian wife of Tucker to help cover his cover story as a businessman while his team executes their high-stakes mission in Tehran.

During the course of the movie, Zara and Tucker develop an emotional and romantic relationship amid the surrounding danger.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Norouzi told Fox News Digital that Levi is a "fantastic actor," adding, "And you do want to be opposite him as the leading lady."

The former "The Traitors" contestant went on to say that Levi was an "awesome" screen partner.

WATCH: ‘The Fix’ star Elnaaz Norouzi says rare chemistry with co-star Zachary Levi made scenes 'really good'

"Honestly, he's one of those guys who just lets you be and lets you do," she said. "But whenever I would like — whenever he would feel like I need something from him in the scene to either understand the scene better or to get that chemistry, he would just give it to me."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"And that kind of understanding and that kind chemistry is quite rare, I feel," Norouzi continued. "And me and Zach really had that and that really helped."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"We had fun on set,"" she added. "It was really good."

"The Fix" premieres in theaters on Sept. 11.

item.title: 2026 NFL season predictions: Division winners, playoff teams and Super Bowl pick revealed
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams are a Super Bowl favorite, but bold 2026 NFL season predictions see them losing the opener and falling short of the title.
item.content:encoded:
Predicting what is about to happen in the 2026 NFL season is impossible, the pseudo-experts will tell you. The league is too volatile, injuries happen and sometimes players surprise us by playing well or poorly.

Hogwash.

This is easy. And let me prove it to you:

I predict the Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams, practically every expert's preseason pick to win the NFC West, are going to struggle early in the season. They definitely aren't going to dominate the San Francisco 49ers in the opener.

RAMS' DISASTER IN AUSTRALIA RAISES THE QUESTION: SHOULD THE TEAM HAVE FOLLOWED THE 49ERS THERE EARLIER?

And, as a team with a lot of new faces, especially on defense, they might even struggle the first month of the season.

Fine, so I jest.

The Rams have already lost their opener to the Niners.

But seriously, the Rams’ ability to rally after their season-opening loss is far from certain given the myriad questions they face: the possibility of NFL suspensions for a couple of players, how well Aaron Donald eventually plays, how healthy Myles Garrett will be later this season and whether they have enough team speed.

"The only reason people wouldn't pick them is because the odds-on favorite to win the Super Bowl traditionally doesn't win the Super Bowl," "NFL RedZone" host Scott Hanson told OutKick.
